proof:
# Projective density changes and optimized integer cap normals

This is a second-order necessary condition at a projective-orbit minimum,
in an explicitly twice-differentiable cap-profile regime. It is NOT claimed
for every convex body or every supporting-facet coincidence. It does not
give the numerical OC bound. It makes a specific negative second-order
term visible beyond the bulk first-moment certificate.

Let d>=1, let P be finite, and let K_p be positive actual fibers. Let mu
be their unweighted volume measure, M its mass, and beta its maximum
normalized depth. Suppose this family is a local minimum under all small
positive affine projective denominators L_t(p)=1+t A(p). On the fixed
original fibers the image volume has density L_t(p)^(-d).

Assume there is only ONE deepest base p_0. Fix any positive critical cap
circuit through its interior maximizing center (p_0,x_0), written

    H_j={a_j.p+u_j.x>=b_j}, |u_j|=1,
    mu(H_j)=Q=beta M,
    rho_j>0, sum rho_j=1, sum rho_j u_j=0.

For each j,p put T_jp=b_j-a_j.p, and let

    F_jp(s)=|K_p intersect {u_j.x>=s}|,
    S_jp=-F_jp'(T_jp),  R_jp=-F_jp''(T_jp).

The notation R means the derivative with respect to the threshold of
the section-area function -F_jp'. ASSUME each F_jp is C2 near T_jp.
Thus R_jp=-F_jp''(T_jp). Strictly full and empty profiles are included
with zero derivatives. An arbitrary tangent-facet profile need not meet
this assumption. Let S_j=sum_p S_jp>0 and

    kappa_j=(rho_j/S_j)/(sum_l rho_l/S_l).

## 1. Section moments and the integer-normal Hessian

The cap H_j minimizes mass among halfspaces through (p_0,x_0). Varying
its integer normal while compensating the threshold at p_0 gives

    sum_p S_jp (p-p_0)=0.                              (1)

Define matrices and vectors, on the linear span of P-p_0,

    V_j=sum_p S_jp (p-p_0)(p-p_0)^T,
    H_j^*= -sum_p R_jp (p-p_0)(p-p_0)^T,
    h_j=sum_p R_jp (p-p_0),
    k_j=-sum_p R_jp.                                  (2)

Here V_j>=0. Also H_j^*>=0: it is the Hessian in the integer normal
of a C2 function which has a local minimum at the selected cap. This
Hessian is distinct from the halfspace denoted H_j.

## 2. Exact covers while both weights and integer cap normals vary

Write A(p)=A(p_0)+b.(p-p_0). For each cap choose ANY integer-normal
velocity c_j. Replace a_j by a_j+t c_j and b_j by

    b_j+t c_j.p_0+s_j(t),

where s_j(0)=0. The threshold in fiber p is consequently

    T_jp+s_j(t)-t c_j.(p-p_0).                       (3)

Choose the s_j(t) by the exact common-mass quantile construction, with
sum_j rho_j s_j(t)=0. The adjusted caps cover the ENTIRE p_0 fiber
plane and all have one common raw mass tau(t). The implicit-function
theorem applies because S_j>0 and the profiles are C2. Fixed slack
circuit covers at all other bases persist for small t.

Put m_A=integral A(p)dmu and B_j=-d integral_(H_j) A(p)dmu. Equation
(1) makes the first derivative in (3) independent of c_j. Therefore

    tau'(0)=sum_j kappa_j B_j,
    v_j:=s_j'(0)=(B_j-tau'(0))/S_j.                  (4)

The comparison tau(t)/M(t) touches beta at the local orbit minimum.
Since the deepest base is unique and t is signed, its first derivative
is zero for every affine A:

    tau'(0)=beta M'(0)=-d beta m_A.                  (5)

No derivative of an actual maximizing point is used here.

## 3. The full second derivative

Differentiating each weighted cap term

    (1+t A(p))^(-d)
       F_jp(T_jp+s_j(t)-t c_j.(p-p_0))

twice and eliminating the s_j'' by their rho-weighted zero sum yields

    tau''(0)=d(d+1) sum_j kappa_j integral_(H_j) A(p)^2 dmu
       +sum_j kappa_j [k_j v_j^2
            +2 c_j.(v_j h_j-d V_j b)+c_j^T H_j^* c_j].          (6)

For a direct check, before summing over j its second-order term is

    d(d+1) integral_(H_j) A^2 dmu
      +2d sum_p A(p) S_jp [v_j-c_j.(p-p_0)]
      -sum_p R_jp [v_j-c_j.(p-p_0)]^2.

The terms with A(p_0) cancel in the kappa-weighted sum, because
sum_j kappa_j S_j v_j=(sum rho_j v_j)/(sum rho_j/S_j)=0.
The remaining cross term in A is -2d c_j.V_j b by (1), giving (6).
This verifies in particular the signs of h_j and H_j^*.

The total mass satisfies M''(0)=d(d+1) integral A^2 dmu. By (5), the
normalization cross terms cancel in the second derivative of tau/M.
Consequently the numerator

    N(A,c)=d(d+1)[sum_j kappa_j integral_(H_j) A^2 dmu
                                   -beta integral A^2 dmu]
       +sum_j kappa_j [k_j v_j^2
            +2 c_j.(v_j h_j-d V_j b)+c_j^T H_j^* c_j]             (7)

must be nonnegative for EVERY affine A and every collection c_j.
Otherwise the actual comparison cover is strictly below beta for small
t, contradicting local minimality of the orbit.

## 4. Optimizing the cap-normal response

Let w_j=d V_j b-v_j h_j. Since the c_j are independently selectable,
(7) implies w_j belongs to the range of H_j^* for every j and A. If
not, choose a null vector of H_j^* with nonzero scalar product with
w_j and scale c_j along it; the expression in (7) becomes arbitrarily
negative while all other terms stay fixed.

On its range, completing the square for a nonnegative symmetric matrix
gives min_c(c^T H_j^* c-2c.w_j)=-w_j^T (H_j^*)^dagger w_j, where
dagger is its inverse on the range and zero on the nullspace. Hence
the explicit necessary inequality is

    d(d+1)[sum_j kappa_j integral_(H_j) A^2 dmu
                                  -beta integral A^2 dmu]
       +sum_j kappa_j k_j v_j^2
       -sum_j kappa_j w_j^T (H_j^*)^dagger w_j >=0               (8)

for every affine A. This is an exact loss term from optimized integer
cap normals. It cannot be discarded in favor of fixed-cap weight
derivatives.

For several deepest bases one instead uses the full second-order
alternative in `candidate a0a4e151af2d0678`, including
all those bases and allowing the balancing weights to depend on the
direction. Inequality (8) for a convenient single group is NOT a valid
replacement in that situation. Nor does this note remove its explicit
C2 profile assumption at supporting facets.

The product-simplex calculation in the separate exact-descent note is
a noninfinitesimal check on the mechanism: proportional integer-normal
motions keep all selected cap budgets exactly constant, while the
projective density change increases total mass. The present formulas
also show the negative covariance term in that example. No conclusion
for arbitrary projective minima follows without a new argument
controlling the quantities in (8).
